title: Error handling and typed throws
hints: Look at the README's 'New syntax' (`throws(E)`, `throw`, `try?`, `do`/`catch`). The starter's signature says plain `throws`; it needs `throws(AgeError)`.

Idea: parseAge is three guards in order (empty → not a number → outside 0...150), each throwing its case; ageOrNil is a single `try?`; message(for:) calls parseAge inside `do` and switches on `error` in `catch`.
Example on other data: `guard pin.count >= 4 else { throw .tooShort }` · `catch { switch error { case .tooShort: ... case .notDigits(let raw): ... } }`.

Near-answer: `guard !text.isEmpty else { throw .empty }`, `guard let age = Int(text) else { throw .notANumber(text) }`, `guard (0...150).contains(age) else { throw .outOfRange(age) }`; success message: `return "age \(try parseAge(text))"`.
